problem: The figure is titled as the filled pixels of the whole trapezoid, but only rows y=2 to y=6 are shown. The polygon also covers y=1: both slanted edges start there, so the span runs from x=1 to x=9 and, under the chapter's own inclusive rule, 9 pixels would be filled at y=1 (y=7 has no crossings because the top edge is horizontal and the slanted edges end there). A student may conclude the polygon has no row at y=1.
fix: Either rename the figure to 'Filled pixels at y=2 to y=6 of the trapezoid' or add the y=1 row with all nine cells filled.

problem: The formula divides by (y₁ − y₀) without saying that it is undefined when y₁ = y₀. The exclusion of horizontal edges is only mentioned two bullets later, so a student can apply the formula to a horizontal edge and get a division by zero.
fix: After the formula add: the formula is valid only when y₁ ≠ y₀; a horizontal edge has y₁ = y₀ and no single crossing x, so it is never entered in the edge table. It also applies only when y lies between y₀ and y₁.

problem: The question says 'A boundary is 4-connected but has a one-pixel diagonal gap'. These two statements contradict each other: a one-pixel diagonal gap is exactly a place where the boundary is not 4-connected, so the setup is confusing even though the answer given is correct.
fix: Rephrase: 'A boundary contains a one-pixel diagonal step, so two boundary pixels touch only at a corner. Why can an 8-connected flood fill cross it while a 4-connected fill cannot?'
